items.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: we had Ralph Collier — do you remember that name? He played drums I remember... So I mean Saturdays and Sundays and Fridays sometimes... so I could work that in.

ctx.x: But eventually you got to do the Bob Crosby, that special?

Well yeah, I had worked a little around, he booked jobs around town. Yeah I still did single engagements, you know, like people would call me and I would do it. In fact I did like regular club dates — what do they call it — jobbing they call it in Chicago, you know private parties and stuff, it was all during that period. Because at least you could sit down and fake something even. A lot of it was society, like Lester Lanin or whatever, but it was rhythmic, and we worked with a guy who, once in a while we’d get…
Because that would be overtime on the weekends?
